key_insight: A low-cost, resident-focused OPAT bundle in a resource-limited Indian hospital scaled eligible outpatient IV antimicrobial treatment to universal use while maintaining safety monitoring.
clinical_relevance: Standardizing education, eligibility screening, and follow-up can improve OPAT uptake and support hospital bed conservation without increasing readmissions in similar LMIC settings.
method: Pre-post quality improvement study at a tertiary hospital in Rishikesh, India
Compared 6 months pre-intervention with 6 months post-implementation
Intervention included resident education, standardized eligibility screening, and telephonic monitoring
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 100% OPAT utilization among eligible encounters after implementation, with 100% adherence to monitoring indicators and no increase in readmissions.
watch_item: Results come from a single-center QI study, so transferability to other hospitals may depend on staffing, training capacity, and follow-up infrastructure.
paper_title: Scaling Safe Resident Driven OPAT bundle in a Lower Middle-Income Country: A Quality Improvement Intervention
